_notes.ERROR: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct: the analyzer consults it to refuse an emission and report a diagnostic (src/ast/real-csharp-analyzer.ts:1066-1067), and `literal-callee-recovery.cs` is a committed fixture whose parse tree contains one — the same ruling as javascript's ERROR row and the php/error-recovery precedent (reported, not turned into a symbol, neighbours survive).

adjudication.why: These 164 entries were an unverified hand-authored claim: completeness-inventory checks that every node type IS classified, never that the classification is right, so a wrong entry is indistinguishable from a right one. This census replaces assertion with measurement for as many as a corpus sample can settle: a type that never occurs is UNTESTED rather than verified, and a type that occurs and contains nothing publishable is confirmed.

absent.meaning: never occurs in the sample — the verdict is untested, not verified

trivial.meaning: occurs and its subtree contains nothing the analyzer publishes — confirmed by measurement

suspect.meaning: occurs AND contains a publishable node; all inspected are structural containers whose contents are published by the nodes inside them (argument holds reads, if_statement holds calls, type_argument_list holds declared-type references, catch_declaration binds a variable). No probable defect found. Containment alone is not a defect, which is why this bucket is reported rather than acted on.

adjudication.caveat: This measures OCCURRENCE and CONTAINMENT, not correctness. It cannot prove a verdict right; it can only say which verdicts were never exercised, and that is the finding. A wider corpus would move types between the buckets — the 48 absent are the ones a larger sample would test first.

_notes.MISSING: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct: tree-sitter marks an ABSENT required token with `isMissing` on the TOKEN'S OWN type, so the string "MISSING" is never a node type a fixture can contain — a `handled_verified` row would read `uncovered: MISSING` forever. The lane's error walk does read `isMissing` off the whole tree (real-csharp-analyzer.ts:1066-1067); every lane in the fleet records that read with this same row, so the class is named here rather than claimed. A node type that no fixture can witness is not evidence, and a bucket has to say which of the two it means.

decisions.question: C# base lists have no keyword distinction (unlike Java's extends/implements); the first entry may be a base class OR an interface.
decisions.resolution: Kind resolved via the optional type-kind companion (typeKinds) built from the cross-file symbol space; unknown external types use the deterministic rule: first base = extends, remaining = implements.

decisions.question: OO family closure #613 (fsharp corpus): how do target-typed new() sites inside collection/array member initializers resolve?
decisions.answer: Through the member ELEMENT type (EnumSettingEntry[] x = [new()] -> EnumSettingEntry); direct field/property initializers use the declared type base; a new() nested in a call argument resolves to nothing. One shared resolver (csharpResolveTargetTypedNew + csharpMemberDeclaredTypeText) now serves the analyzer AND the differential oracle — the old divergent copies shared the self-map blind spot (member NAME read as the type) that F5 could not see. pinned: csd14-array-member-news fixture + csharp/array-member-new-selfmap mutant.

decisions.question: C# review (2026-09-13): the analyzer emitted no bare-identifier edges at all while the oracle audits only calls/instantiates (CONV-CS-1, same both-sides-blind class as pre-review CP1/R1).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: analyzeCSharpBareIdentifierUses resolves Property-kind member names through the lexical class chain (innermost first), transitive bases (capped) and enclosing classes, with walk-order shadowing (methods, blocks, lambdas, local functions, switch arms, queries, catch/foreach/for/using, class frames for primary-ctor params; record positionals deliberately unbound so property reads flow) and the full exclusion discipline (declaration positions incl. leftmost/declarator roles, callees incl. generic/conditional wrappers, member leaves, qualified names, preproc text, labels, attribute names, named/anonymous/with/subpattern designators, deconstruction/out writes, LHS writes, nameof/typeof/default/sizeof and is/as type positions). `uses` is uncompared for csharp, so fixtures + mutants gate it (no oracle change). Fixture csharp/bare-value-reads (10 expects, 12 forbids); mutants drop-bare-uses, reemit-shadowed-reads, reemit-designator-reads CAUGHT.

decisions.question: C# review (2026-09-13): calls in top-level statements (C# 9) were dropped for lack of an enclosing symbol name, while the oracle derives every invocation leaf (each one a MISSING).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: attribute to global (field-use convention). Fixture expects calls global->WriteLine; mutant top-level-call-loss CAUGHT. No oracle change needed (it already derived them).

decisions.question: C# review (2026-09-13): `nameof(x)` parses as an invocation with an identifier callee, so every site fabricated calls->nameof on both sides (probe-verified; the keyword set lacked it).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: nameof added to the analyzer keyword set and the oracle keyword regex; the operand is gated as a name position. Fixture forbids calls NameOf->nameof and uses NameOf->Max; mutant nameof-call-fabrication CAUGHT.

decisions.question: C# review (2026-09-13): both catch forms parse as catch_clause containing an optional catch_declaration — counting the inner declaration counted typed catches but never bare `catch { }`.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: count the clause (exactly once either way) in the file counter and the per-symbol counter (kept in sync per CSD2); matches swift catch_block. Fixture pins Errors/ErrorsTyped complexity 2; mutant bare-catch-complexity-loss CAUGHT.

decisions.question: C# review (2026-09-13): `file class Hidden` reported undefined visibility and exported as public API (probe-verified).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: file maps to private; file-scoped types never export. Fixture expects Hidden private and forbids its export; mutant file-type-exported CAUGHT.

decisions.question: C# review (2026-09-13): positional-pattern heads (`o is Point(1, y)`) parse as invocation_expressions under constant_pattern, so both sides emitted them as calls.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: invocations directly under constant_pattern are patterns (no calls edge; their bare identifiers read as constant patterns, declared vars bind via declaration rules). Fixture forbids calls Pos->Point; oracle mirrored (lane-pinned).

decisions.question: C# second review (2026-09-13): `new Point { X = v }` parses initializers as assignment_expressions — X must designate (never read) while v reads. Probe-verified on a colliding member.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: the assignment-LHS write gate covers initializer designators (verified identical shape); values read normally. Fixture expects Build->G and forbids Build->X/Y; mutant reemit-initializer-designator-reads CAUGHT.

decisions.question: C# second review (2026-09-13): this grammar spells ALL type names plain `identifier` (no type_identifier/field_identifier nodes exist — 17 dead disjuncts removed, audit-proven), so type-parameter lists, where-clause and base-list subtrees and tuple types need explicit gates or member-name collisions fabricate reads.
decisions.resolution: FIXED, partially unpinned: type_parameter_list direct names, where-clause and base-list subtrees, and tuple_type identifiers never read. Unpinnable on valid code by construction (a colliding member in those positions is either invalid code or genuinely ambiguous), so no fixture/mutant covers them — documented with the grammar evidence; lanes + F3 confirm zero valid-code impact.

decisions.question: C# second review (2026-09-13): variable_declarator names bound unconditionally (member declarators self-shadowed their own reads); foreach/deconstruction/lambda binding had gaps (write-position foreach vars, lambda params, typed deconstruction args never bound).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: declaratorRole climb (method-ish = local binds via leftmost-name resolution incl. wrapped declarators; class-ish = member skips) with a matching emission gate; foreach binds type-gated first names plus all-but-first-and-last fallback with a positional write gate; lambdas bind parameter names + implicit params; deconstruction binds typed args (bare args write-skip). Existing forbids cover every class (Shadowed/Flow/Guards pairs); no new mutants needed (drop-bare-uses + reemit-shadowed-reads span the surface).

decisions.question: C# second review (2026-09-13): class-scope reads (member initializers, class-level attribute arguments) attributed to global, and top-level-statement locals had no frame (member-name collisions leaked).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: innermost enclosing class attributes class-scope reads (strictly more precise; field pass unchanged by design); a file-scope frame binds top-level locals. Fixture expects Holder->Limit/Annotated->Other class sources and forbids global->topmark.

decisions.question: CONV-CS-1 (#750, #739/#744 family): bare member reads emitted ZERO uses edges (`return x;`) and chain roots (`inner` in `inner.deeper.leaf`) were missing while deeper leaves emitted — the THIRD analyzer with the same read-attribution blind spot (java #739, javascript #744).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED at this wave's commit: the CS-R1 bare-identifier mechanism (identifier_usage edges via lexical-frame resolution) repairs both recorded shapes; probe-verified live (`uses Get->x`, `uses Read->inner/deeper/leaf`). The issue's own code is the fixture csharp/chain-root-reads (verbatim; root + bare reads pin meta.relationshipType=identifier_usage), and the drop-bare-uses mutant reproduces the pre-CS-R1 state and now fails on it — a live gate, not documentation.

decisions.question: CONV-CS-2 (#751): csharp had NO framework detection at all — metadata.detectedFrameworks undefined (python emits [], java a string): the only language missing both the mechanism and the metadata key, so the family payload contract was not uniform.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: detectCSharpFrameworks (grammar-level markers: using-directive roots incl. static/alias/global forms, base-list leaf names, attribute names) feeds the family-aligned payload — framework (fixed-priority primary), detectedFrameworks (ALWAYS an array, [] when none), frameworkPatterns, hasFrameworkIntelligence. Emitted order is the fixed CS_FRAMEWORK_ORDER so import order can never change the payload; string ops only (no new regex literals). Fixtures csharp/framework-detection (3 simultaneous families + exact payload pin + 5 forbidFrameworks over-match guards) and csharp/framework-none (the [] shell); mutants framework-detection-dropped + framework-overshoot CAUGHT.

The C# component-render construct is the DYNAMIC RENDER HOST: `builder.RenderComponent<Widget>()` (the component is a TYPE ARGUMENT) and `builder.RenderComponent(typeof(OtherWidget))` (the component is a `typeof` ARGUMENT). THE ANALYZER EMITS IT (src/ast/real-csharp-analyzer.ts:2285 and :2315) and the PROOF is the BEHAVIOURAL FIXTURE validation/m14/fixtures/csharp/render-host-component.cs, whose edge exists only when the construct reaches the analyzer as a REAL NODE. THE POPULATION IS ZERO, measured: the whole-admitted-population census counts 51 render-host calls, of which 0 name a component by a type argument and 0 name one by a `typeof` argument - the component-render construct itself is RAZOR's, a different language with a different grammar - and the corpus-wide text search finds 0 files with a render host naming a component in either shape (the only render-shaped text in the corpus is the `RenderFragment<T>` delegate TYPE and the unrelated `RenderArgs<TDocument>`).
